title: Hardwood Floor Refinishing Cost in 2026
description: Find hardwood floor refinishing cost per square foot in 2026, with prices by room size, stain costs, and DIY vs pro totals.

cover.alt: A hardwood floor half sanded to bare wood with a drum sander in the room

takeaways: Pros charge $3 to $8 per square foot to refinish hardwood floors, per Angi 2026 data.
HomeGuide puts the average total at $800 to $3,200 for a typical job.
Stain adds $1 to $3 per square foot, and dustless sanding runs $5 to $8 per square foot.
body:
Professional hardwood floor refinishing costs $3 to $8 per square foot in 2026, based on Angi data. HomeGuide gives a similar range of $2 to $8 per square foot, with an average total of $800 to $3,200. Most of that money is labor, so room size and floor condition drive your quote more than the finish brand does.

## How much does hardwood floor refinishing cost?

Angi breaks the job into three parts. Sanding runs $0.50 to $3 per square foot. Staining, if you change color, adds $1 to $3 per square foot. The finish coats run $1 to $2 per square foot. A natural finish with no stain skips the middle charge.

| Floor area | Low, natural | Typical | High, with stain and repairs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100 sq ft | $200 | $500 | $800 |
| 250 sq ft | $900 | $1,400 | $1,800 |
| 400 sq ft | $1,000 | $2,000 | $2,500 |
| 500 sq ft | $1,500 | $2,500 | $4,000 |
| 1,000 sq ft | $2,000 | $4,000 | $5,000 or more |

Those totals follow the Angi cost table by square footage and the HomeGuide room table. HomeGuide lists a 12 x 12 ft room (144 sq ft) at $290 to $1,000 with no stain, and $430 to $1,200 with stain. A whole house at 1,500 sq ft runs $3,000 to $10,500 with no stain on HomeGuide data.

Wood type shifts the price. Angi lists oak, cherry, and engineered hardwood at $3 to $5 per square foot to refinish. Pine runs $4 to $7, and maple and mahogany run $6 to $8, because hard or soft woods need more care with the sander. Stairs are priced apart, often per step, because each tread is hand work.

A screen and recoat costs less. If your finish is dull but the wood is sound, a pro can scuff the old finish and add a fresh coat with no sanding to bare wood. HomeGuide lists that work at $1 to $3 per square foot. It will not fix deep scratches, gray water marks, or worn spots that reach bare wood.

## Worked example: 500 sq ft of oak with a new stain

Say you refinish a living room and hall that total 500 sq ft (46.5 sq m). The oak is worn but sound. You want a medium stain and three coats of finish, and you hire a pro.

- Base refinishing, sanding and finish, no stain: 500 sq ft x $5 per sq ft = $2,500.
- Stain work: 500 sq ft x $2 per sq ft = $1,000.
- Total: $2,500 + $1,000 = $3,500.

Check the total a second way. The full job at $7 per sq ft, which is inside the $3 to $8 Angi range with stain at the higher end, gives 500 x $7 = $3,500, the same figure. At the low end, a natural finish at $3 per sq ft would cost $1,500. At the high end, dustless sanding with stain at $8 per sq ft would cost $4,000.

Budget one more line if boards need repair. Replacing a few damaged boards before sanding is common in entryways and under sinks. Get that price in writing before sanding starts, because new boards need stain tests to blend with old wood. Use our [flooring calculator](/blog/flooring-calculator/) if you price new boards for the repair.

## What pushes the price up or down?

Floor condition is the first lever. Pet stains that turn wood black, deep gouges, and cupping from water damage need extra sanding passes or board replacement. A floor with light surface wear sands fast and stays at the low rate.

Room layout is next. Open rooms sand with big machines and go fast. Small rooms, closets, and halls need edge sanders and hand work on a larger share of the area. Many pros set a minimum charge, so one tiny room alone costs more per foot than the same room added to a larger job.

Finish choice matters less, but it still counts. Water based finish costs more per gallon and dries fast, so crews can coat twice in a day. Oil based finish costs less per gallon, smells strong, and needs longer between coats. More coats add labor time either way, and each coat should be priced in the quote.

Access and prep add time. Pros charge to move heavy furniture, pull carpet and staples, and remove old baseboard if needed. Empty rooms before the crew arrives and you cut that charge. Our [flooring waste factor](/blog/flooring-waste-factor/) guide helps if you also price new flooring for another room.

## DIY or hire a pro?

DIY refinishing runs about $1 to $2 per square foot in rental and materials for many homeowners. You rent a drum or orbital sander, an edger, and buy abrasives, stain, and finish. A 500 sq ft job might cost $500 to $1,000 out of pocket, plus two or three full days of work.

The risk is the sander. A drum sander left in one spot cuts a dip that shows in low light and is hard to fix. Chatter marks and uneven stain are the two flaws pros get called in to repair most. If your floor is thin, valuable, or badly stained, the pro price is cheaper than a second attempt.

Engineered hardwood needs extra care. It can be refinished only if the top wood layer is thick enough to sand. Thin layers allow one light sanding at most, and some allow none. Ask the pro to check the layer at a floor vent or threshold before you sign. If the floor cannot be sanded, compare replacement with our [laminate vs vinyl plank cost](/blog/laminate-vs-vinyl-plank-cost/) guide.

## How can you save money on refinishing?

Do connected rooms in one visit. One setup, one dust system, and one trip beats three small jobs. If you plan to sell, refinish the main living areas and skip low traffic bedrooms with sound finish.

Pick a natural finish if you like the wood color. Skipping stain saves $1 to $3 per square foot and a full day of dry time. If you do stain, test it on an inconspicuous spot or a spare board first. Stain color on old oak rarely matches the sample card.

Ask if a screen and recoat will do. For floors with dull finish but no bare wood, that job costs half as much and takes a day. A good pro will tell you plainly if your floor is past that point. Get the answer during the quote visit, not after sanding starts.

Keep furniture out for the full cure time the pro gives you. Dragging a sofa back on day two can scar soft finish and force a repair coat. Socks only for the first days, then felt pads under every leg.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to refinish 1,000 square feet of hardwood?
At $3 to $8 per square foot, 1,000 sq ft costs $3,000 to $8,000 as a simple product. Angi's table puts 1,000 sq ft at $2,000 to $5,000 for many standard jobs, with stain and repairs lifting the top end.

### How long does hardwood floor refinishing take?
Most jobs take 2 to 3 days of work, plus dry and cure time. You can often walk in socks after a day or two. Heavy furniture and rugs should wait about a week, based on the finish your pro uses.

### How many times can a hardwood floor be refinished?
Solid hardwood can take several full sandings over its life, often four or more, if enough wood sits above the tongue and groove. Engineered floors depend on the top layer and may allow one sanding or none.

### Is dustless refinishing worth the extra cost?
Angi puts dustless work at $5 to $8 per square foot. The vacuum system cuts airborne dust a lot, which helps with allergies and in occupied homes. It does not cost less, and it does not change the finish quality.

### Should I stain my floors darker to hide damage?
Dark stain hides some color flaws and shows dust and light scratches more. It also adds $1 to $3 per square foot. Test the stain on your own boards first, because old wood takes stain darker than new sample boards.

## Next step

*Prices are US figures from 2026 and vary by region and supplier.*
